strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine efficiency-fidelity gap in dynamic 3DGS with practical importance for real-time applications

Extremely comprehensive experimental evaluation: 50 standardized scenes (MonoDyGauBench), multiple datasets (NeRF-DS, D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, Nerfies, iPhone), careful ablations, 3-run averaging, detailed hyperparameter sensitivity analysis
Strong empirical results: 13.71× faster rendering and 2.53× shorter training while surpassing non-neural baselines in quality (SSIM/MS-SSIM higher than all baselines); exceeds 100 FPS in many cases
Technically sound approach with clear mathematical formulation (TSP gradient-based pruning, GroupFlow SE(3) alignment), each component targeting specific bottleneck
Demonstrates strong synergistic effects: pruned+GroupFlow outperforms individual components, improving both speed and quality in many cases
Honest presentation with clear discussion of limitations, thorough ablation studies, and per-scene analysis enabling assessment of applicability
Practical reproducibility: explicit hyperparameters, multiple metrics, enables memory-constrained training (RTX A5000 vs. requiring larger GPUs)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: TSP is straightforward temporal aggregation of existing Speedy-Splat (Eq. 6), TSS uses ad-hoc temporal perturbation without rigorous justification, GroupFlow applies established SE(3) fitting. Main contribution is combination of existing techniques rather than novel components

TSS mechanism incompletely justified: claim that 'gradient magnitudes implicitly capture temporal inconsistency' is asserted but not rigorously validated; no quantitative analysis of what fraction of removed Gaussians are actually floaters vs. low-sensitivity primitives

Quality degradation with GroupFlow alone: Table 2 shows LPIPS increases (0.283→0.313 on DeformableGS, 0.277→0.380 on 4DGS), suggesting SE(3) rigid motion assumption fundamentally limits non-rigid deformation capture; paper acknowledges but doesn't provide mitigation strategies or detailed failure analysis

Hyperparameter design lacks principled justification: J=2048 chosen to 'balance' but Table 10 shows flat performance across J∈[128,4096]; λr=0.5 lacks ablation; β=0.1, τ=20,000 appear empirically motivated; soft/hard pruning (60%,30%) selection seems arbitrary despite broad optimum in Figure 5

Regularization effect not fully characterized: paper mentions 'mild regularizing effect' from GroupFlow but doesn't formalize; unexpectedly large improvements on iPhone (SSIM 0.46→0.51) suggest regularization is significant, complicating interpretation of GroupFlow's actual contribution
Incomplete memory analysis: model size shown but peak memory usage during training not detailed; important for practitioners assessing practical adoption feasibility

Limited failure case analysis: Section 6 mentions 'highly deformable or non-rigid regions' suffer degradation but provides no concrete examples, quantitative analysis, or specific scenarios where approach breaks down
Equation 5→6 simplification lacks formal justification: claim that second term diminishes 'as training converges' not rigorously proven; could be problematic early in training or with large residuals
Missing statistical analysis: while results average 3 runs, no confidence intervals or significance tests; important where improvements are modest
Comparison scope: no evaluation against very recent methods (MEGA, Swift4D mentioned but not compared); limited to 5 baseline methods in MonoDyGauBench

strengths: Addresses a practical problem: the efficiency-fidelity gap in neural motion field methods with genuine real-time rendering applications
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 50 scenes and 5 datasets with detailed ablations and per-scene metrics
Achieves significant practical speedups (6.78× with pruning, 13.71× with full pipeline) demonstrating effective engineering
Clear presentation with good motivation, effective figures, and well-structured methodology
Complementary components (TSP, TSS, GroupFlow) show synergistic effects through thorough ablation studies
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: TSP extends Speedy-Splat [14] via temporal gradient aggregation (Eq. 6)—straightforward but incremental; TSS adds standard Gaussian perturbation with unjustified hyperparameters; GroupFlow uses standard clustering + Umeyama alignment without empirical comparison to related methods (SC-GS, SPGaussian, RigGS)

Quality degradation inconsistent with claims: LPIPS increases (0.283→0.313 on DeformableGS), contradicting abstract claims of 'preserving superior image quality'; per-dataset results highly variable (D-NeRF GroupFlow FPS decreases unexpectedly; iPhone PSNR drops from 15.13 to 11.83)

Design choices lack principled justification: trajectory similarity weighting λᵣ=0.5 appears arbitrary; fixed J=2048 groups despite varying scene complexity; TSS hyperparameters (β=0.1, τ=20000, linear annealing) are unmotivated; Nmax=100 threshold unexplained

Problematic experimental setup: baselines evaluated on RTX 3090, proposed method on RTX A5000/A6000 (different GPUs complicate FPS comparison); memory efficiency gains conflated with algorithmic efficiency; DeformableGS memory limitations treated as fairness issue
Inadequate analysis of sensitivity approximation (Eq. 5→6): drops second-order residual term assuming convergence without quantifying error or discussing impact across training stages
Insufficient comparison with related motion grouping work: no empirical comparison with SC-GS, SPGaussian, RigGS despite similar goals; unclear why GroupFlow is superior to existing methods

Overclaiming throughout: abstract states 'preserving superior image quality' while LPIPS degrades; claims 'surpassing all baselines in speed while preserving superior image quality' contradicted by Table 2; vague about quality-speed tradeoffs

Superficial limitations discussion: no examples of pruning failures, no analysis of when rigid motion assumption breaks down, no investigation of anomalies like D-NeRF FPS decrease or iPhone quality collapse
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned, critical hyperparameters scattered across main text and appendix, ablation suggests optimal J=1024 on NeRF-DS but J=2048 used throughout

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the real efficiency-fidelity gap in neural dynamic 3DGS, with practical impact enabling real-time rendering at 100+ FPS
Comprehensive evaluation across 50 scenes spanning 5 diverse datasets (D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, NeRF-DS, Nerfies, iPhone) with detailed per-scene metrics and ablation studies

Technically sound approach with three complementary, well-designed modules: TSP extends gradient pruning naturally to temporal domain; TSS cleverly exposes temporally unstable floaters; GroupFlow provides principled distillation via trajectory clustering

Strong empirical results with 6.78× speedup (TSP+TSS) and 13.71× speedup (full pipeline) on DeformableGS while maintaining or slightly improving SSIM/MS-SSIM, demonstrating effective accuracy-efficiency trade-off
Clear presentation with effective figures, precise mathematical formulations, and honest discussion of limitations; extensive supplementary results support reproducibility
Surprising regularizing effect showing GroupFlow can improve quality on noisy scenes, suggesting method discovers meaningful motion structure
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: TSP is straightforward extension of Speedy-Splat to temporal aggregation; TSS uses heuristic annealing schedule (β=0.1, τ=20000) without principled justification; GroupFlow applies classical Umeyama alignment with ad-hoc trajectory weighting (λr=0.5)

Significant GroupFlow limitations not thoroughly analyzed: assumes locally rigid motion with limited evaluation on highly non-rigid scenes; independent quality drop of ~0.5 SSIM; unexplained FPS decrease on D-NeRF baselines; J=2048 appears somewhat arbitrary

Experimental design concerns: different hardware used for baselines (RTX 3090) vs. proposed method (A5000/A6000) confounds speed comparisons; large discrepancies between MonoDyGauBench and standalone SpeeDe3DGS results raise fairness questions; no quantitative comparison with recent related work (RigGS, DynMF, SC-GS)

Technical analysis gaps: Eq. 5→6 simplification assumes convergence but affects early training pruning decisions; limited justification for Gaussian perturbation vs. other noise distributions; trajectory clustering sensitivity to λr and other hyperparameters under-explored; minimal failure case analysis

Missing ablations: no comparison with simpler baselines (reduced MLP capacity, knowledge distillation); memory overhead analysis absent; no user studies or temporal artifact evaluation; multiple hyperparameters appear empirically tuned (soft prune 60%, hard 30%) without systematic sensitivity analysis beyond Figure 5

Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned; different experimental setups per dataset; multiple hand-tuned hyperparameters with limited justification; statistical rigor limited (3 runs averaged, no error bars/confidence intervals)
